title: USD.AI’s $1M CHIP buyback sparks 19% rally amid Elon Musk’s AI warning
summary: But Elon Musk's warning about AI cloud failures has put the industry's financial outlook under scrutiny.
content: USD.AI recently completed a one million dollar CHIP token buyback, which sparked a 19 percent rally in its market value. However, this positive market movement occurs as Elon Musk issues a public warning regarding potential AI cloud failures, casting a shadow of financial scrutiny over the broader artificial intelligence industry.

title: Discord is making public chats searchable on Google: How to opt out
summary: Discord conversations on large public servers will soon reach audiences far beyond their communities, raising privacy concerns.
content: Discord is updating its platform to make public chats searchable on Google, allowing conversations from large public servers to reach a much wider audience. While this change increases visibility, it has also raised significant privacy concerns among users who prefer their discussions to remain confined to their communities. Discord has provided options for users and server owners to opt out of this search indexing feature.
content_ta: Discord-ன் பப்ளிக் சாட்கள் இனி Google-ல் தேடும் வசதியுடன் வரவுள்ளன. இதனால் பெரிய பப்ளிக் சர்வர்களில் நடக்கும் உரையாடல்கள் பலரைச் சென்றடையும். இந்த மாற்றத்தால் தனியுரிமை குறித்த கவலைகள் எழுந்துள்ள நிலையில், பயனர்கள் மற்றும் சர்வர் உரிமையாளர்கள் இந்த தேடல் வசதியிலிருந்து விலகிக்கொள்ள (opt out) Discord வழிவகை செய்துள்ளது.

content: Clearstream, the post-trade business of Deutsche Börse, has announced a new initiative to support tokenised fund distribution. The move allows asset managers to securely issue and manage tokenised fund shares utilizing distributed ledger technology. This development marks a significant step forward in integrating blockchain innovations into traditional financial market infrastructures.
content_ta: Deutsche Börse-ன் போஸ்ட்-ட்ரேட் வணிகமான Clearstream, டோக்கனைஸ்டு ஃபண்ட் விநியோகத்தை ஆதரிப்பதற்காக ஒரு புதிய திட்டத்தை அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த நகர்வு சொத்து மேலாளர்கள் டிஸ்ட்ரிபியூட்டட் லெட்ஜர் தொழில்நுட்பத்தைப் பயன்படுத்தி டோக்கனைஸ்டு ஃபண்ட் பங்குகளை பாதுகாப்பாக வெளியிடவும் நிர்வகிக்கவும் அனுமதிக்கிறது.

title: Zumo and Quantum Chain partner up to fight quantum threats
summary: Cryptocurrency firm Zumo has joined forces with quantum blockchain platform Quantum Chain in efforts to combat the growing threat of quantum attacks.
content: Cryptocurrency firm Zumo has partnered with quantum blockchain platform Quantum Chain. The collaboration aims to address and combat the growing cybersecurity threat posed by future quantum computing attacks within the digital asset ecosystem, enhancing the overall security of blockchain technology.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சி நிறுவனமான Zumo, குவாண்டம் பிளாக்செயின் தளமான Quantum Chain உடன் கூட்டு சேர்ந்துள்ளது. எதிர்கால குவாண்டம் கணினி தாக்குதல்களின் வளர்ந்து வரும் அச்சுறுத்தலை எதிர்த்துப் போராடுவதையும், டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து சுற்றுச்சூழல் அமைப்பில் பிளாக்செயின் தொழில்நுட்பத்தின் பாதுகாப்பை பலப்படுத்துவதையும் இந்த ஒத்துழைப்பு நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: DOSH Adds Google Pay to Extend Digital Wallets to Underbanked Users
summary:
The FCA-regulated prepaid account, built for financially excluded consumers, now supports contactless Android payments without a credit check.
The post DOSH Adds Google Pay to Extend Digital Wallets to Underbanked Users appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: DOSH, an FCA-regulated prepaid account designed for financially excluded and underbanked consumers, has integrated Google Pay. This addition enables users to make seamless contactless Android payments without requiring a credit check, further expanding digital wallet accessibility for underserved populations.
content_ta: நிதி ரீதியாக பின்தங்கிய பயனர்களுக்காக உருவாக்கப்பட்ட FCA-regulated ப்ரீபெய்ட் கணக்கான DOSH, Google Pay சேவையை இணைத்துள்ளது. இந்த புதிய வசதியின் மூலம், கிரெடிட் செக் தேவையில்லாமல் பயனர்கள் காண்டாக்ட்லெஸ் Android பேமெண்ட்களை மேற்கொள்ள முடியும்.

title: Securitize adds Stellar blockchain as institutional tokenization gathers steam
summary: The firms announced the agreement at Meridian 2026, the Stellar Development Foundation’s annual conference in Portugal.
content: Securitize has integrated the Stellar blockchain to expand its institutional tokenization offerings. The partnership was announced at the Meridian 2026 conference, hosted by the Stellar Development Foundation in Portugal. This collaboration highlights the growing adoption of blockchain technology for institutional asset tokenization.
content_ta: Securitize நிறுவனம் தனது நிறுவன அளவிலான tokenization சேவைகளை விரிவுபடுத்த Stellar blockchain-ஐ இணைத்துள்ளது. Portugal நாட்டில் நடைபெற்ற Stellar Development Foundation-ன் வருடாந்திர மாநாடான Meridian 2026-ல் இந்த ஒப்பந்தம் அறிவிக்கப்பட்டது.

title: Justin Sun now holds 2.82% of PEPE supply – The biggest individual holder
summary: PEPE draws fresh attention as Justin Sun’s holdings outpace perpetual Futures Open Interest.
content: Justin Sun has emerged as the largest individual holder of PEPE, now owning 2.82% of the cryptocurrency's total supply. This massive accumulation has drawn fresh attention to the token, particularly as Sun's holdings outpace the perpetual Futures Open Interest, highlighting significant interest and trading dynamics surrounding the asset in the current market.
content_ta: Justin Sun தற்போது PEPE-ன் மிகப்பெரிய தனிப்பட்ட ஹோல்டராக உருவெடுத்துள்ளார், இவர் இப்போது கிரிப்டோகரன்சியின் மொத்த சப்ளையில் 2.82% வைத்துள்ளார். இந்த பெரிய அளவிலான சேகரிப்பு PEPE மீது புதிய கவனத்தை ஈர்த்துள்ளது, குறிப்பாக Sun-ன் ஹோல்டிங்ஸ் பெர்ச்சுவல் ஃபியூச்சர்ஸ் ஓபன் இன்ட்ரெஸ்ட்டை விஞ்சியுள்ளது குறிப்பிடத்தக்கது.

title: The Autumn Budget 2026 – How FinTech holds the answers to Burnham’s biggest problems
summary:
UK FinTech urges the government to back SME lending, AI in financial services, investment and sterling stablecoins in the upcoming Budget to drive growth, jobs and financial inclusion nationwide.
The post The Autumn Budget 2026 – How FinTech holds the answers to Burnham’s biggest problems appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: Ahead of the Autumn Budget 2026, UK FinTech leaders are urging the government to support SME lending, artificial intelligence in financial services, and sterling stablecoins. The sector argues that these measures are essential to drive economic growth, create jobs, and improve financial inclusion nationwide, presenting financial technology as a key solution to pressing economic challenges.
content_ta: Autumn Budget 2026-க்காக காத்திருக்கும் நிலையில், SME கடன் வழங்குதல், நிதி சேவைகளில் artificial intelligence மற்றும் sterling stablecoins ஆகியவற்றை அரசு ஆதரிக்க வேண்டும் என UK FinTech தலைவர்கள் வலியுறுத்துகின்றனர். நாடு முழுவதும் பொருளாதார வளர்ச்சி, வேலைவாய்ப்புகள் மற்றும் நிதி உள்ளடக்கத்தை மேம்படுத்த இந்த நடவடிக்கைகள் மிகவும் அவசியమని இத்துறை வாதிடுகிறது.

title: Nearly 90% of large businesses are embracing tokenized cash to speed up payments: DBS
summary: Stablecoins lead instruments in use or planned at 63%, ahead of tokenized deposits at 53% and tokenized money market funds at 52%.
content: A recent DBS study reveals that nearly 90% of large businesses are adopting tokenized cash to accelerate payment processes. Stablecoins are leading this trend, with 63% of organizations currently using or planning to use them. Meanwhile, tokenized deposits and tokenized money market funds are also seeing strong interest, adopted or planned by 53% and 52% of large enterprises respectively.
content_ta: பெரிய வணிக நிறுவனங்களில் கிட்டத்தட்ட 90% நிறுவனங்கள் பணப் பரிவர்த்தனைகளை விரைவுபடுத்த டோக்கனைஸ்டு பணத்தைப் பயன்படுத்தி வருவதாக DBS-இன் சமீபிய ஆய்வு தெரிவிக்கிறது. இந்தத் துறையில் ஸ்டேபிள்காயின்கள் முன்னணியில் உள்ளன, 63% நிறுவனங்கள் இவற்றை ஏற்கனவே பயன்படுத்துகின்றன அல்லது பயன்படுத்தத் திட்டமிட்டுள்ளன. மேலும், டோக்கனைஸ்டு டெபாசிட்டுகள் மற்றும் டோக்கனைஸ்டு மணி மார்க்கெட் ஃபண்டுகளும் முறையே 53% மற்றும் 52% நிறுவனங்களால் பயன்படுத்தப்படுகின்றன.

title: Brazil’s largest lender becomes first bank to formalize crypto brokerage under new rules
summary: Itaú Unibanco notified Brazil’s central bank of its crypto trading and custody operations on Tuesday, ahead of an Oct. 30 deadline.
content: Brazil’s largest lender, Itaú Unibanco, has become the first bank to formalize its crypto brokerage operations under new regulatory rules. The institution officially notified Brazil’s central bank regarding its crypto trading and custody services ahead of the upcoming regulatory deadline, marking a major step for traditional banking integration with digital assets in the country.
content_ta: Brazil-ன் மிகப்பெரிய வங்கியான Itaú Unibanco, புதிய ஒழுங்குமுறை விதிகளின் கீழ் தனது crypto brokerage சேவைகளை முறைப்படுத்திய முதல் வங்கி என்ற பெருமையை பெற்றுள்ளது. வரவிருக்கும் விதிமுறை கெடுவிற்கு முன்பாக, தனது crypto வர்த்தகம் மற்றும் custody சேவைகள் குறித்து Brazil-ன் மத்திய வங்கிக்கு அந்த நிறுவனம் அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாக அறிவித்துள்ளது.

title: Kospi surges 7% as SK Hynix earnings fuel AI stock rebound
summary: South Korean chipmakers led a broader AI recovery after SK Hynix reported a sevenfold profit surge and announced another $45 billion in shareholder returns.
content: The Kospi index surged 7% following a strong recovery in artificial intelligence stocks, led by South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix. The massive market rebound was driven by SK Hynix reporting a significant profit increase and announcing substantial shareholder returns, boosting investor confidence across the technology sector.
content_ta: SK Hynix நிறுவனத்தின் லாப உயர்வு மற்றும் முதலீட்டாளர் லாபப்பகிர்வு அறிவிப்பால், செயற்கை நுண்ணறிவு துறை பங்குகள் மீண்டெழுந்ததை அடுத்து Kospi குறியீடு 7% உயர்ந்தது. இந்த சந்தை எழுச்சி தொழில்நுட்பத் துறை முதலீட்டாளர்களின் நம்பிக்கையை அதிகரித்துள்ளது.

title: Bitcoin price eyes $82K as Morgan Stanley strategist says most of correction is over
summary: Bitcoin sought to rebuild support at $80,000 while Asian and US tech stocks extended a rebound into key corporate earnings releases.
content: Bitcoin is eyeing a move toward $82,000 as a Morgan Stanley strategist suggests the majority of the recent correction has concluded. During this period, Bitcoin worked to rebuild support around the $80,000 mark. Meanwhile, technology stocks in both Asia and the United States extended their ongoing market rebound ahead of several critical corporate earnings reports.
content_ta: Morgan Stanley-ன் மூலோபாய நிபுணரின் கூற்றுப்படி, சமீபத்திய விலை சரிவு முடிவுக்கு வந்துள்ளதை அடுத்து Bitcoin விலை $82,000-ஐ எட்டும் என்று எதிர்பார்க்கப்படுகிறது. இந்த காலகட்டத்தில் Bitcoin $80,000 என்ற ஆதரவு நிலையை மீட்க முயன்றது. இதற்கிடையில், வரவிருக்கும் நிறுவனங்களின் லாப அறிக்கைகளை முன்னிட்டு, ஆசிய மற்றும் United States தொழில்நுட்பப் பங்குகள் தங்கள் சந்தை உயர்வைத் தொடர்ந்தன.

title: Coinbase Customer Data Hit in Analytics Vendor Breach, Funds ‘Not Impacted’
summary: The incident at analytics firm Amplitude hit a "small subset" of Coinbase customers, the exchange said, without saying how many.
content: Cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase experienced a data breach affecting a small subset of its customers following an incident at its analytics vendor, Amplitude. Coinbase assured users that their funds remain entirely safe and unaffected by the breach. The company did not disclose the exact number of customers impacted by the vendor security issue.
content_ta: அனலிட்டிக்ஸ் வெண்டரான Amplitude-ல் ஏற்பட்ட தரவு மீறல் காரணமாக, Coinbase-ன் வாடிக்கையாளர்களில் ஒரு சிறிய பகுதியினர் பாதிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளனர். வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் நிதிகள் முற்றிலும் பாதுகாப்பாக இருப்பதாகவும், இந்தச் சம்பவத்தால் அவை பாதிக்கப்படவில்லை என்றும் Coinbase உறுதிப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இதனால் பாதிக்கப்பட்ட வாடிக்கையாளர்களின் சரியான எண்ணிக்கையை நிறுவனம் வெளியிடவில்லை.

title: MEXC and Hacken Launch AI Trading Safety Handbook to Promote Safer AI Adoption
summary: Mutsamudu, Comoros, October 28, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, and blockchain security, compliance, and regulatory assurance partner Hacken, have released the MEXC × Hacken AI Trading Safety Handbook, providing practical guidance on how users and platforms can use and deploy AI-assisted and automated trading tools more safely, from research and decision support through trade execution. The handbook follows the recent MEXC AI Trading Report, which found strong interest in AI alongside clear demand for greater control. In MEXC’s 2026 survey, willingness to use automated trading rose from 55% to 71.8% when limits on funds, positions, leverage and losses were introduced. As AI takes a more active role in trading, the handbook emphasizes that safety cannot rely on the AI model alone. AI-facilitated actions should be checked against separate permissions, financial limits and risk controls before execution. It covers risks including credential exposure, excessive permissions, manipulated data and unintended execution, while outlining practical safeguards for both users and platforms. For users, the handbook sets out five safety checks: Ask, Verify, Limit, Control and Review. For platforms, it outlines five principles: Guard, Limit, Approve, Controls and Test. Together, they provide a practical framework for expanding the use of AI while keeping appropriate controls in place. “AI can make trading more accessible and efficient, but greater capability should come with stronger safeguards,” said Vugar Usi Zade, CEO of MEXC. “At MEXC, we want users to benefit from innovation, while taking a measured approach to AI adoption. Our People First principle means giving users access to new capabilities without losing sight of control, transparency and risk.” ““AI agents will soon place more orders than people do. Trust in them should be earned the way smart contracts earned it: through independent controls, continuous red-teaming and evidence anyone can verify.”,” said Dyma Budorin, CEO and co-founder of Hacken. “This handbook is intended to raise awareness of those risks and provide practical support for both users and platforms. As adoption grows, platforms will need to test these safeguards continuously and strengthen them as new risks emerge.” MEXC and Hacken hope the handbook can serve as a practical reference for users and platforms as AI becomes more deeply integrated into trading, helping raise risk awareness and support safer, more responsible adoption across the industry.   About MEXC Founded in 2018, MEXC is a leading global multi-asset trading platform built as your 0-fee gateway to infinite opportunities. Serving users across 170+ markets, MEXC provides simple and efficient access to crypto, stocks, tokenized assets, derivatives, and a growing range of TradFi-linked opportunities through one account and one gateway. With 0 trading fees, deep liquidity, broad asset coverage, and a high-performance trading experience, MEXC is designed for retail users who want to discover earlier, act faster, and trade with fewer barriers. As crypto and traditional finance continue to converge, MEXC is committed to making global opportunities more accessible, helping users trade freely and MEXCmize every opportunity. MEXC Official Website｜ X ｜ Telegram ｜How to Sign Up on MEXC   About Hacken Hacken is a security and assurance partner for financial institutions and the infrastructure they rely on: exchanges, ecosystems, custodians, banks, asset managers, and tokenization platforms. Hacken’s AI security work includes AI agent security audits and red-teaming of AI systems. Founded in 2017, Hacken has 60+ engineers and more than 1,500 clients across industries, including the European Commission, ADGM, Ethereum Foundation, Societe Generale-Forge, MetaMask, and Bybit. Hacken website | X | LinkedIn   For media inquiries, please contact MEXC PR team: media@mexc.com
content: MEXC and Hacken have launched the MEXC × Hacken AI Trading Safety Handbook to promote safer AI adoption in digital asset trading. The handbook provides practical guidance for users and platforms to deploy AI-assisted tools securely, emphasizing risk controls, financial limits, and independent verifications. This initiative follows survey findings indicating strong interest in automated trading alongside a clear demand for enhanced user control and safety safeguards.
content_ta: MEXC மற்றும் Hacken இணைந்து டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து வர்த்தகத்தில் AI இன் பாதுகாப்பான பயன்பாட்டை மேம்படுத்தும் வகையில் 'AI Trading Safety Handbook' கையேட்டை வெளியிட்டுள்ளன. இந்த கையேடு, பயனர்கள் மற்றும் தளங்கள் AI-உதவி பெறும் வர்த்தகக் கருவிகளைப் பாதுகாப்பாகப் பயன்படுத்த நடைமுறை வழிகாட்டுதல்களை வழங்குகிறது. ஆபத்துக் கட்டுப்பாடுகள் மற்றும் நிதி வரம்புகளின் அவசியத்தை இது வலியுறுத்துகிறது.

title: SUN.io Completes 52nd Buyback and Burn: Total SUN Burned Surpasses 685M as SunSwap Accelerates Ecosystem Integrations
summary: Through its recurring buyback and burn program, SUN.io continues to channel protocol revenue from SunSwap, SunPump, and SunX into SUN token value accrual, while accelerating SunSwap’s cross-platform integrations to reinforce decentralized liquidity.  SUN.io, the core DeFi liquidity infrastructure on the TRON network, has successfully executed its 52nd SUN token buyback and burn on October 27, removing more than 7.23 million SUN from circulation. This round marks the platform’s 52nd consecutive burn, bringing the cumulative total to over 685 million SUN tokens, valued at more than $11 million. title: From Instant Payments to Agentic AI: How Form3 and AWS Are Shaping the Future of Payments
summary:
At Sibos 2026 in Miami Beach, Financial IT spoke with Jose Zapata Petrov, Vice President and Head of Global Partnerships at Form3, and Nilesh Dusane, Global Head of Institutional Payments at AWS, about the technologies transforming the global payments landscape.
The discussion explores the continued expansion of instant payments, the emergence of tokenised deposits, and the potential of generative and agentic AI to reshape payment operations. Petrov and Dusane also discuss how the Form3–AWS partnership is helping financial institutions modernise their payment infrastructure, strengthen operational resilience and develop innovative, customer-focused financial services.
Instant Payments and the Evolution of Money Movement
Jose Zapata Petrov, Vice President and Head of Global Partnerships, Form3: The payments landscape is evolving rapidly, from the expansion of instant payments to the emergence of agentic AI. How do you see the industry developing, and what role can technology partners such as Form3 and AWS play in this transformation?
Nilesh Dusane, Global Head of Institutional Payments, AWS: The payments industry has experienced several major catalysts that have changed how businesses and consumers move money.
One of the most significant developments has been the expansion of instant payment schemes. Over the past five to six years, we have seen schemes such as FedNow and RTP in the United States, SEPA Instant Payments in Europe, and Faster Payments in the UK gain momentum. Financial institutions need to connect to these payment networks and offer instant payment services to their customers.
This is where partnerships with companies such as Form3 become particularly important. By running and scaling its payment infrastructure on AWS, Form3 can help financial institutions bring new payment capabilities to market more quickly.
We are also seeing growing interest in tokenisation, including tokenised deposits, which offer additional ways to move money. These developments are not necessarily competing with instant payments; they serve different needs and are likely to coexist.
For technology providers such as AWS and Form3, this creates an opportunity to help financial institutions build the infrastructure and services needed to support a broader range of payment methods.
Tokenised Deposits and New Payment Rails
Jose Zapata Petrov, Form3: Tokenisation is attracting increasing attention across financial services, with tokenised deposits and other digital payment models gaining traction. How do you see these developments shaping the future of money movement?
Nilesh Dusane, AWS: Instant payments continue to expand globally, with around 70 to 80 countries rolling out or developing instant payment capabilities.
At the same time, tokenisation is emerging as another important development. Greater regulatory clarity, including developments surrounding the GENIUS Act in the United States, has contributed to growing interest in stablecoins and tokenised deposits. We have also seen industry initiatives exploring tokenisation-based payment solutions.
From the customer’s perspective, the key benefit is choice. Different payment methods can serve different use cases, depending on the requirements of the transaction and the service being delivered.
Instant payments will continue to play an important role, while tokenisation may create additional opportunities for moving money. We expect these approaches to coexist, giving financial institutions greater flexibility in how they design and deliver payment services.
For AWS and Form3, the priority is to help our financial institution customers develop the technology capabilities needed to support these evolving requirements.
Generative AI and Value-Added Financial Services
Jose Zapata Petrov, Form3: Beyond payment infrastructure, artificial intelligence is creating new opportunities across financial services. How is the role of generative AI evolving, particularly in payments and the services financial institutions can offer their customers?
Nilesh Dusane, AWS: Over the past two to three years, generative AI has prompted financial institutions to rethink their businesses at multiple levels.
Initially, much of the focus was on productivity, including helping developers and business users work more efficiently. Financial institutions have since begun exploring how generative AI can support fraud prevention, improve internal operations and identify potentially fraudulent activity more proactively.
We are now seeing another stage of development: using AI to deliver value-added services to customers.
Rather than offering only a basic payment or banking service, financial institutions can use AI to provide capabilities such as accounts receivable and accounts payable reconciliation, as well as cash flow forecasting. These services can help customers manage their finances and operations more effectively.
For technology providers, AI also creates an opportunity to help financial institutions develop and deploy these capabilities more quickly, accelerating the delivery of new services.
Agentic AI, Compliance and Operational Resilience
Jose Zapata Petrov, Form3: As the industry moves towards agentic AI, where do you see the greatest opportunities for financial institutions, particularly in areas such as compliance, observability and operational resilience?
Nilesh Dusane, AWS: Agentic AI presents an opportunity to build on the progress already made with generative AI.
Financial institutions could use AI agents to support activities such as meeting compliance obligations, improving observability and managing other operational processes. These applications could help institutions work more efficiently while strengthening their ability to monitor and manage complex payment environments.
The broader opportunity is to combine these capabilities with modern payment infrastructure to improve operational resilience and enhance the services financial institutions can deliver.
As institutions explore agentic AI, the focus should remain on practical applications that address real operational challenges and deliver measurable value to customers.
The Form3–AWS Partnership
Jose Zapata Petrov, Form3: Form3 and AWS have been working closely together as Form3 expands into new markets and develops new capabilities. How does the partnership help financial institutions respond to these changes and bring modern payment solutions to market?
Nilesh Dusane, AWS: The partnership between Form3 and AWS brings together cloud technology and specialised payment infrastructure to help financial institutions develop and scale modern payment services.
As payment schemes expand and new technologies emerge, institutions need infrastructure that can support evolving requirements without making innovation unnecessarily complex.
Form3’s payment platform, running on AWS, helps financial institutions connect to payment networks and bring new capabilities to market. The partnership also creates opportunities to explore emerging technologies, including agentic AI, and to use the tools and support available through the AWS partner ecosystem.
Ultimately, our approach is centred on working backwards from the customer: understanding the challenges financial institutions face and helping them build solutions that address those needs.
As the payments landscape continues to evolve, collaboration between cloud providers and specialist technology partners will remain important in helping financial institutions innovate, strengthen resilience and deliver greater value to their customers.

title: Saviynt Recognised in 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Privileged Access Management

We believe Saviynt’s recognition in 2026 is evidence of its continued investment.
The recognition comes as the definition of privileged access continues to expand. Cloud workloads, automation, non-human identities and AI agents all require elevated access, creating a need for organisations to govern and secure privilege beyond traditional administrator accounts while reducing persistent access.
“Privilege is no longer limited to a defined group of administrators. As AI agents and machine identities become mainstream in enterprises, organisations need to understand the context of why access is needed, how long it should be granted, and who is accountable for it,” said Anirudh Sen, Senior Vice President of Products at Saviynt. “We believe our repeated recognition in the Gartner PAM research reflects our commitment to securing the full Privilege Spectrum through a unified identity security platform that brings identity governance and privileged access together.”
Solving privilege challenges in the AI era requires a new approach with market-leading identity lifecycle management. Saviynt believes that a modern PAM solution must combine identity governance, privilege lifecycle management, lifecycle automation, and time-bound, just-in-time access. A unified platform that brings IGA and PAM together can simplify administration, deliver a more seamless customer experience, and help organisations secure access at the pace of AI adoption.
Built on Zero Trust principles, Saviynt takes a continuous, risk-based approach to privilege management. By advancing Zero Standing Privilege (ZSP), Saviynt helps organizations minimise persistent elevated access and ensure privileges are granted only when justified by context and risk. Its Privilege Spectrum framework enables organisations to apply the right level of access at the right time while maintaining security and productivity.

title: Ripple Treasury Introduces Always-On Corporate Treasury Platform to Modernize Corporate Cash Management

Unveiled at Swell 2026, the announcement marks a significant step toward always-on corporate treasury, bringing together established treasury management functionality, AI-powered orchestration and digital rail infrastructure.
As AI accelerates financial decision-making and digital payment rails enable money to move beyond traditional banking hours, businesses need treasury operations that can keep pace. At the center of the new Ripple Treasury experience is an orchestration layer that works with GSmart, Ripple Treasury's treasury-native AI capabilities, to coordinate and automate workflows across cash positioning, forecasting, reconciliation, liquidity management, and payments. By connecting decisions with execution, Ripple Treasury helps finance teams reduce manual processes, respond faster to changing financial needs, and move toward truly always-on treasury operations.
“Treasury is moving from visibility to action, and the emerging challenge is orchestration: connecting trusted data, intelligence and the ability to move money so that better decisions turn into timely execution,” says Kevin Permenter, Research Director of IDC. “Platforms that bring those layers together, rather than assembling them across providers, are addressing the constraint that matters most.”
Over the past year, 46% of organizations increased their U.S. cash balances, while 86% of treasury professionals said their organizations would choose real-time money market funds if they met their investment policies, according to the 2026 AFP Liquidity Survey. There is an emerging opportunity for businesses to manage cash more productively without compromising their liquidity requirements.
One of the ways Ripple Treasury is meeting this need is the introduction of 24/7 Returns, a new capability designed to help eligible corporate customers generate returns on operating cash that would otherwise remain idle overnight, over weekends, and during holidays. Ripple Treasury customers may earn returns on their qualifying digital assets held in a Ripple wallet including RLUSD, Ripple's U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin, subject to meeting program requirements. Businesses can put eligible cash to work beyond traditional banking hours without independently managing the underlying digital asset transactions.
“When one of the core tenets of your business is payment accuracy and security, you have to have an incredible partner and ecosystem,” says Blake Tablak, CEO of Trax. “Our partnership with Ripple Treasury is just getting started and already returning value.”
"The way businesses move money is changing, and treasury needs to evolve with it," said Renaat Ver Eecke, Senior Vice President of Ripple Treasury. "As AI accelerates decision-making and digital rails enable money to move around the clock, businesses need systems that can keep pace. Our vision is to bring treasury management, intelligence, and execution together, giving finance teams the ability to act faster and operate continuously without adding complexity or sacrificing control."
The launch builds on Ripple's broader strategy to connect corporate finance with modern financial infrastructure. By bringing together treasury management, payments, liquidity, stablecoins, and custody, Ripple aims to give enterprises a more integrated way to manage and move money across fiat and digital rails. Rather than requiring businesses to assemble and manage multiple disconnected providers, Ripple offers a single partner for increasingly complex treasury operations, helping reduce operational friction and simplify the adoption of digital assets.

title: NatWest Cuts Marketing Compliance Approval Times by 80% With Adclear’s AI Agents
summary:
Adclear, the provider of agent-driven compliance infrastructure for the financial services sector, has today announced a partnership with NatWest to overhaul how compliance is embedded across its marketing and communications operations, allowing the bank to scale content production without compliance becoming the bottleneck.
The move comes as FCA interventions on financial promotions have doubled year on year, while the volume of marketing content financial services firms need to review continues to grow. Compliance teams typically spend a huge amount of time reviewing assets by hand, often pushing campaign launches back by three to five days - a gap that widens every time marketing output scales faster than manual review can follow.
NatWest has built up product marketing across current accounts, credit cards, loans, mortgages and savings over many years, with each product line historically supported by its own review process and tooling. As the bank has moved to centralise its marketing operations onto a single workflow system, that fragmentation has become a bottleneck: more content flowing through fewer, more central compliance teams, with the risk of slowing the business down rather than speeding it up. Adclear is folding its AI compliance checks into NatWest's marketing approvals process as part of that centralisation, retiring a patchwork of legacy tools and manual sign-off in favour of a single, tech-first standard for reviewing content across the business.
Adclear consolidates NatWest's infrastructure into one platform, screening website, social, marketing and advertising content in real time and flagging where copy, creative or disclosures fall short of relevant regulations before it goes live. Integrated directly into NatWest's Workfront workflow system, it gives everyone involved in sign-off a single, consistent review process across every product line and channel, rather than requiring separate tools and separate sign-off for each.
The rollout builds on NatWest's existing five-year data and AI transformation programme with Accenture, which is also supporting the integration of Adclear's compliance checks into the bank's wider technology estate.
For a bank operating at NatWest's scale, serving around 20 million customers, the shift from fragmented legacy systems to one centralised platform is designed to remove duplication, cut review times and give compliance teams a clear, consistent audit trail - all without slowing down the pace at which marketing needs to publish. Since integration, NatWest has cut approval times for marketing content by 80%, allowing campaigns to move from review to market in a fraction of the time it previously took.
The partnership positions Adclear as the compliance standard other UK financial institutions are increasingly measuring themselves against, as marketing and communications teams across the sector come under pressure to scale AI-generated content without slowing compliance down.
Adclear's AI is relied on by marketers from across the financial sector to ensure that financial promotions adhere to relevant regulations, whilst providing an in-depth audit trail for compliance teams. Its technology is already used by Monzo, Lloyds Banking Group, PensionBee, IG Group, Freetrade, Yonder, Trade Nation, ActivTrades, Ocean Finance, Flagstone and Blockchain.com.
Matthew Harwood, Head of Marketing and Engagement Platforms at NatWest, said:
“Adclear has helped us turn compliance from something that slowed marketing down into something that actively supports how fast we can move. Cutting our approval times by 80% has let our teams focus on producing better, more relevant content rather than waiting on sign-off, and that speed is now a genuine advantage in how quickly we can get campaigns to customers. This is exactly the kind of technology-led transformation we want running across the bank.”

Doni Hoti, CEO and co-founder of Adclear, said:
"Financial promotions compliance hasn't kept pace with how much content marketing teams now produce - output across the sector has grown roughly tenfold over the past decade, while most firms are still running the same manual, email-based approval chains they always have. The rules were never the bottleneck, the process around them was. NatWest recognised that early, and this partnership is what happens when a bank decides to fix the process itself rather than manage around it.”

title: MarCoPay Partners With Sumsub to Strengthen Fraud Prevention for Filipino Seafarers and Support AFASA Compliance
summary:
Sumsub brings identity verification, AML screening, and transaction monitoring together for MarCoPay, providing a unified view of real-time fraud signals to help address the Philippines’ enhanced anti-scam requirements.
Sumsub is partnering with MarCoPay, a Philippines-based electronic platform for seafarers and their families, to support customer onboarding, ongoing compliance checks and transaction monitoring in line with the Philippines’ Anti-Financial Account Scamming Act (AFASA) requirements. By providing a connected view of the real-time fraud signals across the customer journey, this enables MarCoPay to strengthen continuous fraud prevention and risk management processes.
MarCoPay enables seafarers to securely manage, access and transfer their funds through a digital ecosystem designed for speed, reliability and convenience. Its approach combines accessible payment services with compliance and fraud prevention controls, reflecting its commitment to financial security and consumer protection.
 
The Philippines remains the world’s leading supplier of seafarers, reinforcing the need for secure financial services that protect a globally mobile workforce and their families. According to Sumsub’s Identity Fraud Report 2025-26, deepfake attacks in the country increased 61% year-on-year in 2025—one of the highest rates in the Asia-Pacific region—while sophisticated multi-step coordinated fraud rose 180% year-on-year globally, highlighting the growing challenge posed by AI-enabled fraud. AFASA’s enhanced fraud-management requirements, which took effect in June 2026, further raise the bar for real-time monitoring and fund-recovery controls across financial institutions.
“This partnership strengthens our ability to deliver safe and secure services,” said Hayato Kiyohara, CEO of MarCoPay. “With enhanced security, we aim to better serve Filipino seafarers and our business partners.”
Serving Filipino seafarers through its electronic payments platform, MarCoPay uses Sumsub’s document-based identity verification, Liveness Detection and AML Screening to support secure customer onboarding. With the ability to verify over 14,000 types of identity documents from more than 220 countries and territories, Sumsub provides the global coverage needed to support seafarers whose work regularly takes them across borders.
Powered by Sumsub’s proprietary Liveness Detection, MarCoPay can authenticate genuine users in seconds while helping detect spoofing attempts and deepfakes. The technology creates a 3D FaceMap to confirm that a user is physically present during verification and continuously references it for authorizing all future actions, such as logins and transactions, strengthening defences against AI-enabled impersonation and fraud.
MarCoPay uses Sumsub’s AML Screening to conduct sanctions, politically exposed person (PEP), watchlist and adverse media checks through a single workflow. The solution draws on more than 50,000 data sources across over 240 countries and territories, supporting MarCoPay’s compliance processes as it scales.
This integrated set of controls supports MarCoPay’s fraud prevention efforts in line with the AFASA requirements. Sumsub’s AFASA Fraud Management Bundle complements these measures by enabling transaction monitoring through rule-based fraud detection and dynamic risk scoring. It helps MarCoPay identify and respond promptly to suspicious transactions, including the fund-recovery processes.
“AFASA is reshaping how financial institutions in the Philippines approach fraud prevention, placing greater focus on connected controls across the customer lifecycle. This makes an operational layer that unifies verification, fraud prevention, transaction monitoring, and risk workflows increasingly critical,” said Penny Chai, Vice President, APAC at Sumsub. “Our partnership with MarCoPay reflects Sumsub’s commitment to supporting Philippine businesses as the compliance landscape evolves. By providing that trust infrastructure needed to build multi-layered defences against AI-enabled fraud, we help businesses build a more resilient response to emerging fraud risks.”

title: Lovey Announces £250M Senior Secured Credit Facility With Pollen Street Capital
summary:
Lovey, the UK’s fastest-growing fintech and financial services provider, specialising in SME lending and brokerage, has today announced a senior secured credit facility of up to £250 million with Pollen Street Capital (“Pollen Street”), an alternative asset manager. The facility is made up of £50 million committed capital and a £200 million accordion, making it the largest funding facility in Lovey's history and marking a key milestone in the company's growth.
 
The facility demonstrates continued institutional investor confidence in Lovey's lending model, technology and long-term strategy and reinforces Lovey's position as a leading finance provider focusing on SME funding. The facility will significantly increase Lovey’s lending capacity, supporting the business as it scales its own-book lending while continuing to grow its established brokerage proposition.
 
Founded by Jack Smith in 2016, Lovey has grown from a one-person start-up into a 120-strong business, funding more than £600 million in loans to over 11,000 UK SMEs. Built around a mission to make lending simple, fast and beautiful, Lovey has expanded rapidly while staying focused on making finance easier and more accessible for small businesses. The new facility will support that mission by giving Lovey the capital to help more UK SMEs access funding quickly and flexibly.
 
Lovey began lending directly from its own balance sheet in 2022, building on its experience as a broker to develop a deeper understanding of the funding needs of UK SMEs. Today, the business combines direct lending with its established brokerage proposition, giving customers access to both Lovey’s own lending and a wider panel of funding partners. This approach allows Lovey to match businesses with the funding solution that best suits their needs, while the new facility provides greater capacity to grow its direct lending operation.
 
Jack Smith, Founder and CEO at Lovey, comments:
 
“This new facility is an important milestone for us and will enable us to put more capital behind UK small businesses, scale our own-book lending and give more SMEs access to finance when they need it. Pollen Street shares our belief that finances for small businesses should be simpler, faster and more flexible, and we’re really pleased to have them backing Lovey for this next stage of growth.”
 
Kai Hunter, Chief Operating Officer at Lovey, comments:
 
“The funding announced today is the result of close and collaborative work with Pollen Street and I am grateful to their team, and to our own, for the diligence they brought to it. This funding deepens our lending capacity and allows us to offer larger loans, so that we can back more of the UK’s small and medium-sized businesses, from those that have found finance hardest to secure to the well-established, with greater speed and certainty.”
 
Ethan Saggu, Investment Director, Pollen Street, adds:
 
“Lovey has spent almost a decade seeing the UK SME lending market from a broker’s perspective, giving the team an expert view of where demand for credit is going unmet. We have financed a number of specialist SME lenders and recognise what it takes to grow from brokerage into balance-sheet lending. Lovey has done so with a well-defined product and a focused approach, and we look forward to supporting the team as it scales.”
 
Lovey was advised by Ashurst Perkins Coie and Pollen Street was advised by Simmons & Simmons.
 
The facility builds on Lovey's existing funding arrangements announced last year, including a £35 million revolving credit facility from Paragon Bank and a £10 million junior medium-term note programme from LGB Capital Markets. The new facility also adds to Lovey's growing institutional funding base as it enters its next phase of expansion.
